subject: Term adjustment & burst capacity plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Term adjustment & burst capacity plan

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive renewal call yesterday. Per our conversation I’m sending a concise proposal for the renewal window and the ramp/burst options HelioMeds asked about. Key points below and I attached an updated term sheet (Redwood_TermSheet_v3.pdf) and our Q4 usage forecast for reference.

Summary (proposed):
- Term: 12 month renewal (start 2028-01-01) with option to extend for +6 months at a pre-agreed uplift rate.
- Committed capacity: 300k token units / month (baseline).
- Burst capacity: up to 600k token units / month billed at a blended overage rate; we can configure monthly burst caps so cost is predictable.
- Staggered invoicing option: we can support quarterly invoicing or split monthly tranches (we typically mirror your fiscal cadence).

As next steps: can you confirm whether Procurement needs the private offer to present a single annual PO or three quarterly POs? If they prefer a single PO we’ll route a Private Offer (AWS marketplace) acceptance path and coordinate DocuSign for signatures. If staggered POs are needed we’ll adjust invoices and acceptance windows accordingly.

Kimberly/Karthik — looping you in to handle marketplace acceptance logistics and the billing cadence.

Thanks,
Mateo
--

Mateo —

Appreciate the summary. Procurement prefers to keep a single annual PO if possible (simpler for our SAP flows), but we need the invoice schedule to be able to accept an annual PO with quarterly invoices. Can Redwood issue an annual PO acceptance that maps to quarterly invoice dates?

A few items we’ll need before we can sign:
1) A clean term sheet with payment milestones and the billing cadence called out explicitly (we use that as an attachment to the PO).
2) Tax treatment and remit instructions for Redwood (we need W-9 or equivalent).
3) Confirmation of start date and when the first invoice will be generated.
4) DocuSign link or platform to sign the acceptance.

We’re also seeing a higher-than-expected Q4 forecast; can you confirm the burst rate and whether you’ll cap overages automatically once we hit the agreed monthly burst cap?

Attaching our PO template for your legal team to review: HelioMeds_PO_template.docx

Best,
Procurement
HelioMeds

Hi Procurement / Samantha —

Thanks for the clarity. We can absolutely accept an annual PO and break invoices into quarterly invoices on our side — Redwood will generate quarterly invoices that reference the annual PO number you supply. That flow is supported for Private Offers in AWS and we’ll also replicate the invoice cadence for direct billing if that’s preferred.

Regarding the burst overage: we will configure a soft cap and an automated alert at 90% of the burst threshold, and a hard cap if you want enforced throttling (we can enable or disable hard caps per account). If you prefer we’ll keep hard caps off and bill overages at the blended overage rate in the term sheet. Please confirm which approach your team prefers.

Action items for us to complete asap:
- Redline the HelioMeds PO template (I’m attaching a redline suggestion).
- Confirm tax docs: Mateo, can you trigger legal/finance for W-9 and remit details?
- Marketplace acceptance: AWS, can you confirm the typical acceptance window when a Private Offer has staggered invoice mapping? We want to ensure HelioMeds can accept the offer without interruption.

Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Sales Operations

Hi everyone —

Quick update following Kimberly’s notes.

1) DocuSign / acceptance: Here’s the DocuSign link for the final Private Offer acceptance + term sheet: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/StartSigning.aspx?docusign=abc123def (expires 2027-12-01). Please sign the term sheet and we’ll submit the Private Offer to AWS within 24 hours of signed acceptance.

2) Invoicing cadence: We will accept a single annual PO from HelioMeds and generate quarterly invoices (Jan / Apr / Jul / Oct). The first invoice date will be 2028-01-05. All invoices will reference the annual PO number and include line items for baseline committed capacity and an explicit burst overage line.

3) Tax / remit: Finance is attaching our W-9 and remit instructions in the DocuSign envelope; if Procurement needs those separately I can send to procurement@heliomeds.com.

4) Burst enforcement: We default to soft caps + alerts. If you want a hard cap to avoid any accidental overage charges, please reply-all and request ‘hard cap ON’. Otherwise we’ll leave hard cap OFF and bill at the blended overage rate specified in the term sheet.

Attachments: Redwood_TermSheet_v3.pdf (PDF), usage_forecast_HelioMeds_Q4.csv (CSV)
